key_insight: Quantum impurity solvers could enable more accurate screening of strongly correlated oxygen-electrode materials for solid oxide fuel and electrolysis cells.
engineering_relevance: The framework links interface energetics and conductivity to electrode performance through oxygen exchange, transport, microstructure, and thickness.
method: Screen candidate materials with DFT and construct correlated impurity models from electrode–electrolyte interfaces.
Use GW+DMFT or SEET embedding with quantum solvers for finite-temperature impurity Green’s functions.
Connect microscopic observables to continuum electrode models and deployment-based business-value estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract provides illustrative logical-qubit counts and proposes benchmarks based on converged vacancy and migration energetics and comparisons with leading applicable classical solvers.
watch_item: Quantum advantage remains unproven; full resource estimates must include thermal-state preparation, simulation, measurement, and repeated solves.
paper_title: Screening strongly correlated materials in solid oxide cells with quantum simulation
